intro: Hi! Today you'll learn the words you need to talk about the news: air pollution and plastic rubbish, tourists and local culture, floods, droughts and volcanoes. We'll practise them in real Indonesian situations, from the haze in Kalimantan to the tourists at Borobudur. Warm-up: what's the biggest environmental problem in your city?
teachingNotes: Teach the words in small themed groups with an Indonesian gloss and practise them in sentences, not only as translations. Environment: pollution (polusi, pencemaran; pollute = verb, polluted = adjective), air pollution, rubbish (British) = trash / garbage (American) = sampah, waste (limbah, sampah; general and a bit formal, both varieties: plastic waste, food waste), plastic, climate change (perubahan iklim: changes in weather patterns over many years) vs global warming (pemanasan global: the Earth getting hotter, one part of climate change), deforestation (penggundulan hutan), endangered animals (hewan yang terancam punah: orangutans, the Komodo dragon), protect (melindungi), save energy (menghemat energi), reduce / reuse / recycle (mengurangi / memakai ulang / mendaur ulang).

The node's first common error is *'We must recycling plastic' → We must recycle plastic. After must, should, have to, can and will, use the base verb (bentuk dasar, no -ing, no to after must/should): must recycle, should save, have to protect. Learners mix it up because 'recycling' is also a common noun (Recycling is important.). Also stress that pollution, rubbish, trash, waste and plastic (the material) are uncountable: a lot of pollution, not *'many pollutions'. Reuse vs recycle: reuse = use the same thing again (refill a bottle, use a jar for sugar); recycle = the material is made into something new (old bottles become new plastic).

Tourism and culture: tourist (wisatawan, the person) vs tourism (pariwisata, the industry). The node's second common error is *'Many tourist come to Bali' → Many tourists (Indonesian doesn't mark plurals: banyak turis). Objek wisata is a tourist attraction, never *'tourism object'. Recap from a2-vocab-travel (don't reteach): go sightseeing, buy souvenirs, take photos, visit a temple. New: local culture (budaya setempat), tradition (tradisi), ceremony (upacara), heritage site (situs warisan budaya; Borobudur and Prambanan are UNESCO World Heritage Sites), respect local customs (menghormati adat setempat; at the airport 'Customs' = bea cukai, a different meaning), overtourism (terlalu banyak wisatawan: an idea people discuss for parts of Bali). Wisatawan mancanegara = foreign tourists; wisatawan domestik = local / domestic tourists.

Extreme weather: flood (banjir; also a verb: It often floods in January), drought (kekeringan, often after a long dry season = kemarau panjang; said 'draut'), heatwave (gelombang panas: a period much hotter than normal for that place), storm (badai), landslide (tanah longsor), earthquake (gempa bumi), volcano (gunung berapi) + erupt (meletus): Mount Merapi erupts, forest fire (kebakaran hutan) and haze (kabut asap: smoke, not fog). Traps: *'Jakarta is flood' → There's a flood in Jakarta / Jakarta floods; *'big rain' → heavy rain (hujan deras); *'the volcano exploded' is understood but erupted is the normal verb.

Facts: keep them general and true. Don't give statistics, rankings or dates (e.g. don't say Jakarta is 'the most polluted city in the world'). Indonesia is hot all year, so don't call normal Indonesian heat a heatwave; use Europe or India in heatwave examples. Haze comes from forest and peatland fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan, mostly in the dry season.

Limits: A0–A2 grammar only (present simple and continuous, past simple and continuous, present perfect, will, going to, zero and first conditionals, should / must / have to, comparatives, quantifiers). No passive (say 'People cut down the forests', not 'The forests are cut down'), no second conditional, no relative clauses, no past perfect. Don't add more topic words (carbon footprint, renewable energy, biodiversity, tsunami, hurricane) unless the learner asks.

keyPoints.title: Environmental problems and solutions
keyPoints.explanation: Problems: pollution (air pollution), rubbish (British) = trash / garbage (American), plastic waste, climate change, global warming, deforestation, endangered animals. Solutions: reduce, reuse, recycle, protect, save energy. pollution, rubbish and waste are uncountable (a lot of pollution). After must, should, have to and can, use the base verb: We must recycle plastic, not 'must recycling'.

examples.en: Air pollution is a big problem in Jakarta.
examples.id: Polusi udara adalah masalah besar di Jakarta.

examples.en: Orangutans are endangered, so we have to protect their forests.
examples.id: Orangutan terancam punah, jadi kita harus melindungi hutan mereka.

examples.en: You should turn off the lights to save energy.
examples.id: Sebaiknya kamu mematikan lampu untuk menghemat energi.

id.title: Masalah lingkungan dan solusinya
id.explanation: Masalah: pollution (polusi; air pollution = polusi udara), rubbish (British) = trash / garbage (Amerika) = sampah, plastic waste (sampah plastik), climate change (perubahan iklim), global warming (pemanasan global), deforestation (penggundulan hutan), endangered animals (hewan yang terancam punah). Solusi: reduce (mengurangi), reuse (memakai ulang), recycle (mendaur ulang), protect (melindungi), save energy (menghemat energi). pollution, rubbish dan waste tidak bisa dihitung (a lot of pollution). Setelah must, should, have to dan can, pakai kata kerja bentuk dasar: We must recycle plastic, bukan 'must recycling'.

keyPoints.title: Tourism and culture
keyPoints.explanation: tourist = the person (many tourists: add -s), tourism = the industry. A place tourists visit is a tourist attraction (not 'tourism object'). Culture words: local culture, tradition, ceremony, heritage site (Borobudur is a UNESCO World Heritage Site), respect local customs. Overtourism = too many tourists in one place. From A2: go sightseeing, buy souvenirs, visit a temple.

examples.en: Many tourists come to Yogyakarta for its culture and food.
examples.id: Banyak wisatawan datang ke Yogyakarta karena budaya dan makanannya.

examples.en: Tourism brings a lot of jobs to Lombok.
examples.id: Pariwisata membawa banyak lapangan kerja ke Lombok.

examples.en: Please respect local customs when you visit a village.
examples.id: Tolong hormati adat setempat saat kamu mengunjungi sebuah desa.

id.title: Pariwisata dan budaya
id.explanation: tourist = orangnya (wisatawan; banyak wisatawan = many tourists, tambah -s), tourism = industrinya (pariwisata). Objek wisata = tourist attraction (bukan 'tourism object'). Kata budaya: local culture (budaya setempat), tradition (tradisi), ceremony (upacara), heritage site (situs warisan budaya; Borobudur adalah Situs Warisan Dunia UNESCO), respect local customs (menghormati adat setempat). Overtourism = terlalu banyak wisatawan di satu tempat. Dari A2: go sightseeing, buy souvenirs, visit a temple.

keyPoints.title: Extreme weather
keyPoints.explanation: flood (also a verb: it floods), drought (a long time with no rain; said 'draut'), heatwave (a period much hotter than normal), storm, landslide, earthquake, a volcano erupts, forest fire, haze (smoke from fires). Say 'There's a flood in Jakarta' or 'Jakarta floods', not 'Jakarta is flood'. Hujan deras = heavy rain, not 'big rain'.

examples.en: After two days of heavy rain, many streets in Jakarta flooded.
examples.id: Setelah hujan deras dua hari, banyak jalan di Jakarta kebanjiran.

examples.en: There was a strong earthquake in Lombok last night.
examples.id: Ada gempa bumi kuat di Lombok tadi malam.

examples.en: The haze from the forest fires is very bad today.
examples.id: Kabut asap dari kebakaran hutan sangat parah hari ini.

id.title: Cuaca ekstrem
id.explanation: flood (banjir; juga kata kerja: it floods), drought (kekeringan: lama sekali tidak ada hujan; dibaca 'draut'), heatwave (gelombang panas: masa yang jauh lebih panas dari biasanya), storm (badai), landslide (tanah longsor), earthquake (gempa bumi), a volcano erupts (gunung berapi meletus), forest fire (kebakaran hutan), haze (kabut asap dari kebakaran). Katakan 'There's a flood in Jakarta' atau 'Jakarta floods', bukan 'Jakarta is flood'. Hujan deras = heavy rain, bukan 'big rain'.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: Everyone should saving energy at home.
acceptableAnswers: everyone should save energy at home
everybody should save energy at home
assessment.rubric: Correct: Everyone should save energy at home (should + base verb). 'should to save' = 30 (no to after should). 'should saves' = 30. 'must save' = 70 (correct grammar but changes the meaning). Unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word: Jakarta has a lot of air ___ because of the traffic and the factories. On bad days the sky is grey and people wear masks.
assessment.rubric: Correct: pollution (air pollution = polusi udara). 'polution' (spelling) = 80. 'pollutions' = 60 (pollution is uncountable). 'polluted' or 'pollute' = 40 (right family, wrong word type). 'dirty' or 'smoke' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with reduce, reuse or recycle: Rina always takes her own bag to the supermarket because she wants to ___ the amount of plastic she uses.
assessment.rubric: Correct: reduce (use less plastic = mengurangi). 'reduces' = 50 (after to, use the base verb). 'reuse' = 20 (she reuses her bag, but the sentence is about the amount of plastic: less = reduce). 'recycle' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: In August, Labuan Bajo is full of foreign tourist.
acceptableAnswers: in august labuan bajo is full of foreign tourists
labuan bajo is full of foreign tourists in august
assessment.rubric: Correct: … full of foreign tourists (full of + plural; Indonesian 'penuh wisatawan asing' has no plural mark). 'foreign tourism' = 10. 'foreigns tourists' = 50 (adjectives never take -s). Unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: Monas is a famous tourism object in Jakarta.
acceptableAnswers: monas is a famous tourist attraction in jakarta
monas is a famous tourist spot in jakarta
monas is a famous attraction in jakarta
assessment.rubric: Correct: Monas is a famous tourist attraction in Jakarta ('objek wisata' = tourist attraction). 'tourist spot' is fine. 'tourism attraction' = 60. 'tourist object' = 20 (object is still the Indonesian-style word). 'tourism place' = 30. Unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word: Too much water is a flood. Too little water for a long time, when there is no rain for months and the rice fields become dry, is a ___.
assessment.rubric: Correct: drought (kekeringan). 'draught' or 'drout' (spelling) = 70. 'dry season' = 40 (kemarau is the season; the problem is a drought). 'heatwave' = 20 (that's a period of very hot weather).

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word: Mount Merapi ___ again last night. Hot ash and smoke went high into the sky, and people in nearby villages left their homes.
assessment.rubric: Correct: erupted (a volcano erupts = meletus; last night = past simple). 'erupts' or 'erupt' = 50 (right verb, wrong tense). 'exploded' = 60 (understood, but erupt is the normal verb for a volcano). 'broke' or 'burst' = 10.

blocks.text:
These are the words you hear in the news about the **environment** (lingkungan):
- **pollution** = the air, water or land becomes dirty and dangerous. **Air pollution** is the dirty air you see in Jakarta on bad days. The verb is **pollute** (Cars pollute the air.) and the adjective is **polluted** (a polluted river).
- **rubbish** (British) = **trash** or **garbage** (American) = the things you throw away. **Waste** is a more general, slightly formal word used everywhere: *plastic waste, food waste*.
- **plastic** = the material: *plastic bags, plastic bottles*.
- **climate change** = changes in the weather patterns of the world over many years; **global warming** = the Earth getting hotter, one part of climate change.
- **deforestation** = people cut down forests and don't plant them again (for example, for farms or plantations).
- **endangered animals** = animals in danger of disappearing for ever. In Indonesia: **orangutans** and the **Komodo dragon**.

id.text:
Ini kata-kata yang sering kamu dengar di berita tentang **environment** (lingkungan):
- **pollution** = polusi, pencemaran: udara, air atau tanah jadi kotor dan berbahaya. **Air pollution** (polusi udara) adalah udara kotor yang kamu lihat di Jakarta saat sedang parah. Kata kerjanya **pollute** (mencemari: *Cars pollute the air.*) dan kata sifatnya **polluted** (tercemar: *a polluted river*).
- **rubbish** (British) = **trash** atau **garbage** (Amerika) = sampah, barang yang kamu buang. **Waste** (limbah, sampah) lebih umum dan sedikit resmi, dipakai di mana-mana: *plastic waste* (sampah plastik), *food waste* (sisa makanan yang terbuang).
- **plastic** = plastik (bahannya): *plastic bags, plastic bottles*.
- **climate change** = perubahan iklim: pola cuaca dunia berubah selama bertahun-tahun; **global warming** = pemanasan global: Bumi makin panas, salah satu bagian dari perubahan iklim.
- **deforestation** = penggundulan hutan: orang menebang hutan dan tidak menanamnya kembali (misalnya untuk ladang atau perkebunan).
- **endangered animals** = hewan yang terancam punah, bisa hilang selamanya. Di Indonesia: **orangutan** dan **komodo** (Komodo dragon).

rows.id: Polusi udara adalah masalah besar di Jakarta.

rows.en: Climate change is making the weather more extreme.
rows.id: Perubahan iklim membuat cuaca makin ekstrem.

blocks.text:
**No -s on these words.** pollution, rubbish, trash, garbage, waste and plastic (the material) are **uncountable**: you can't count them one by one, like water and rice. So say **a lot of pollution** and **too much rubbish**, not *'many pollutions'* or *'rubbishes'*. To count, use the things: *two plastic bags, three bottles*.

**British or American?** rubbish (UK) = trash / garbage (US). Both are correct; just be consistent.

id.text:
**Tanpa -s untuk kata-kata ini.** pollution, rubbish, trash, garbage, waste dan plastic (bahannya) **tidak bisa dihitung** (uncountable): tidak bisa dihitung satu per satu, seperti air dan nasi. Jadi bilang **a lot of pollution** dan **too much rubbish**, bukan *'many pollutions'* atau *'rubbishes'*. Kalau mau menghitung, sebut bendanya: *two plastic bags, three bottles*.

**British atau Amerika?** rubbish (UK) = trash / garbage (US). Dua-duanya benar; pakai salah satu secara konsisten.

options: There are many pollutions in big cities.
There is a lot of pollution in big cities.
blocks.explain: pollution is uncountable, so it has no -s and goes with a lot of (or much), not many.

id.explain: pollution tidak bisa dihitung, jadi tanpa -s dan dipakai dengan a lot of (atau much), bukan many.

blocks.text:
What can we do? Learn these verbs:
- **reduce** = use **less**: *reduce plastic* (take your own bag, say no to straws).
- **reuse** = use **the same thing again**: *reuse a bottle* (fill it again), *reuse a jar*.
- **recycle** = the material becomes **something new**: old bottles go to a recycling bin and a factory makes new plastic from them. *Recycle* = mendaur ulang.
- **protect** = keep safe: *protect the forests, protect endangered animals*.
- **save energy** = use less electricity: turn off the lights and the AC.

We often use them with **must, should, have to** and **can**. After these words, use the **base verb** (bentuk dasar: the verb with no -s, no -ing, no -ed): *We **must recycle**. You **should save** energy. We **have to protect** the forests.*

id.text:
Apa yang bisa kita lakukan? Pelajari kata kerja ini:
- **reduce** = mengurangi, memakai **lebih sedikit**: *reduce plastic* (bawa tas sendiri, tolak sedotan).
- **reuse** = memakai ulang **barang yang sama**: *reuse a bottle* (diisi lagi), *reuse a jar* (toples).
- **recycle** = mendaur ulang: bahannya diolah jadi **barang baru**. Botol bekas masuk ke tempat sampah daur ulang, lalu pabrik membuat plastik baru darinya.
- **protect** = melindungi: *protect the forests, protect endangered animals*.
- **save energy** = menghemat energi, memakai listrik lebih sedikit: matikan lampu dan AC.

Kata-kata ini sering dipakai dengan **must, should, have to** dan **can**. Setelahnya, pakai **kata kerja bentuk dasar** (tanpa -s, tanpa -ing, tanpa -ed): *We **must recycle**. You **should save** energy. We **have to protect** the forests.*

rows.en: I always take my own bag to reduce plastic.
rows.id: Saya selalu membawa tas sendiri untuk mengurangi plastik.

rows.en: My mother reuses old jars for sugar and coffee.
rows.id: Ibu saya memakai ulang toples bekas untuk gula dan kopi.

rows.en: This factory recycles old bottles into new ones.
rows.id: Pabrik ini mendaur ulang botol bekas jadi botol baru.

rows.en: We have to protect the forests in Sumatra.
rows.id: Kita harus melindungi hutan di Sumatra.

rows.en: You should turn off the AC when you leave the room.
rows.id: Sebaiknya kamu matikan AC saat keluar kamar.

blocks.text:
**'must recycling' is wrong.** You see *recycling* everywhere (*Recycling is important.* = Daur ulang itu penting), so it's tempting to write *'We must recycling'*. But after **must, should, have to, can, will** the verb is always the base form: **We must recycle plastic.** And no *to* after must or should: not *'should to recycle'*.

**Reuse or recycle?** If you use the **same thing** again, it's **reuse**. If the material goes to a factory and becomes **something new**, it's **recycle**. Indonesian *daur ulang* = recycle only.

id.text:
**'must recycling' itu salah.** Kata *recycling* ada di mana-mana (*Recycling is important.* = Daur ulang itu penting), jadi orang tergoda menulis *'We must recycling'*. Tapi setelah **must, should, have to, can, will**, kata kerjanya selalu bentuk dasar: **We must recycle plastic.** Dan tidak ada *to* setelah must atau should: bukan *'should to recycle'*.

**Reuse atau recycle?** Kalau kamu memakai **barang yang sama** lagi, itu **reuse**. Kalau bahannya dibawa ke pabrik dan jadi **barang baru**, itu **recycle**. *Daur ulang* dalam bahasa Indonesia = recycle saja.

blocks.prompt: Budi drinks his coffee from the same metal bottle every day. Which sentence is right?
blocks.explain: He uses the same bottle again and again: reuse. Recycle means the bottle becomes new material in a factory, and reduce means using less of something.

id.prompt: Budi minum kopi dari botol logam yang sama setiap hari. Kalimat mana yang benar?
id.explain: Dia memakai botol yang sama berulang kali: reuse. Recycle berarti botolnya diolah di pabrik jadi bahan baru, dan reduce berarti memakai sesuatu lebih sedikit.

blocks.text:
In A2 you learned to **go sightseeing**, **buy souvenirs** and **visit a temple**. Now let's talk about tourism like in the news:
- **tourist** = the **person** (wisatawan, turis). Two or more: **tourists**. **Foreign tourists** come from other countries; **local** (or **domestic**) **tourists** are from Indonesia.
- **tourism** = the **industry** (pariwisata): hotels, tours, restaurants. *Tourism brings jobs to Bali.*
- **tourist attraction** = a place tourists visit (objek wisata): *Monas, Kota Tua, Lake Toba*.
- **local culture** (budaya setempat), **tradition** (tradisi), **ceremony** (upacara: *a wedding ceremony, a temple ceremony in Bali*).
- **heritage site** = an important old place from history (situs warisan budaya). **Borobudur** and **Prambanan** are **UNESCO World Heritage Sites**.
- **respect local customs** = follow the rules and habits of the place (menghormati adat setempat).
- **overtourism** = too many tourists in one place: people discuss it for parts of Bali (traffic, rubbish, water problems).

id.text:
Di A2 kamu sudah belajar **go sightseeing** (jalan-jalan melihat tempat wisata), **buy souvenirs** dan **visit a temple**. Sekarang kita bicara pariwisata seperti di berita:
- **tourist** = **orangnya** (wisatawan, turis). Dua atau lebih: **tourists**. **Foreign tourists** = wisatawan mancanegara; **local** (atau **domestic**) **tourists** = wisatawan domestik.
- **tourism** = **industrinya** (pariwisata): hotel, tur, restoran. *Tourism brings jobs to Bali.* (Pariwisata membawa lapangan kerja ke Bali.)
- **tourist attraction** = objek wisata, tempat yang dikunjungi wisatawan: *Monas, Kota Tua, Danau Toba*.
- **local culture** (budaya setempat), **tradition** (tradisi), **ceremony** (upacara: *a wedding ceremony* = upacara pernikahan, *a temple ceremony in Bali* = upacara di pura).
- **heritage site** = situs warisan budaya, tempat bersejarah yang penting. **Borobudur** dan **Prambanan** adalah **Situs Warisan Dunia UNESCO**.
- **respect local customs** = menghormati adat setempat: ikuti aturan dan kebiasaan tempat itu.
- **overtourism** = terlalu banyak wisatawan di satu tempat: orang membicarakannya untuk sebagian daerah di Bali (macet, sampah, masalah air).

blocks.text:
**Three Indonesian traps:**
- *banyak turis* has no plural mark, but English needs **-s**: **many tourists**, not *'many tourist'*.
- *objek wisata* is **tourist attraction**, not *'tourism object'*.
- **tourist** (a person) and **tourism** (the industry) are different words: *Tourism is important for Bali. Tourists love Bali.*

**customs** has two meanings: **local customs** = adat, kebiasaan; at the airport, **Customs** = bea cukai.

id.text:
**Tiga jebakan bahasa Indonesia:**
- *banyak turis* tidak punya tanda jamak, tapi bahasa Inggris perlu **-s**: **many tourists**, bukan *'many tourist'*.
- *objek wisata* = **tourist attraction**, bukan *'tourism object'*.
- **tourist** (orang) dan **tourism** (industri) itu kata yang berbeda: *Tourism is important for Bali. Tourists love Bali.*

**customs** punya dua arti: **local customs** = adat, kebiasaan; di bandara, **Customs** = bea cukai.

blocks.prompt: Pak Hasan works for the government. His job is to bring more visitors to Lombok. Complete: Pak Hasan works in ___.
blocks.explain: He works in the industry (pariwisata), so it's tourism. A tourist is one person who visits, and tourists are the visitors themselves.

id.prompt: Pak Hasan bekerja di pemerintahan. Tugasnya mendatangkan lebih banyak pengunjung ke Lombok. Lengkapi: Pak Hasan works in ___.
id.explain: Dia bekerja di bidang industrinya (pariwisata), jadi tourism. A tourist adalah satu orang yang berkunjung, dan tourists adalah para pengunjungnya.

blocks.text:
Indonesia knows extreme weather well. Learn the words in pairs:
- **flood** (banjir) — also a verb: *It often floods in January.*
- **drought** (kekeringan) = no rain for a long time, so there isn't enough water. It often comes after a long dry season (kemarau panjang). Said **'draut'**, like *out*.
- **heatwave** (gelombang panas) = a period of weather much hotter than normal **for that place**. Indonesia is hot all year, so normal hot days are not a heatwave; Europe and India sometimes have heatwaves in summer.
- **storm** (badai), **heavy rain** (hujan deras: not *'big rain'*).
- **landslide** (tanah longsor): soil and rocks slide down a hill, often after heavy rain.
- **earthquake** (gempa bumi).
- **volcano** (gunung berapi) + **erupt** (meletus): *Mount Merapi erupts quite often.*
- **forest fire** (kebakaran hutan) and **haze** (kabut asap): smoke from fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan, mostly in the dry season. Haze is smoke, not **fog** (kabut dari air).

id.text:
Indonesia kenal betul cuaca ekstrem. Pelajari kata-katanya berpasangan:
- **flood** (banjir) — juga kata kerja: *It often floods in January.* (Sering banjir di bulan Januari.)
- **drought** (kekeringan) = lama sekali tidak ada hujan, jadi air tidak cukup. Sering terjadi setelah kemarau panjang. Dibaca **'draut'**, seperti *out*.
- **heatwave** (gelombang panas) = masa cuaca yang jauh lebih panas dari biasanya **untuk tempat itu**. Indonesia panas sepanjang tahun, jadi hari panas biasa bukan heatwave; Eropa dan India kadang mengalami heatwave di musim panas.
- **storm** (badai), **heavy rain** (hujan deras: bukan *'big rain'*).
- **landslide** (tanah longsor): tanah dan batu meluncur turun dari bukit, sering setelah hujan deras.
- **earthquake** (gempa bumi).
- **volcano** (gunung berapi) + **erupt** (meletus): *Mount Merapi erupts quite often.*
- **forest fire** (kebakaran hutan) dan **haze** (kabut asap): asap dari kebakaran di Sumatra dan Kalimantan, kebanyakan di musim kemarau. Haze itu asap, bukan **fog** (kabut dari uap air).

rows.en: After two days of heavy rain, many streets in Jakarta flooded.
rows.id: Setelah hujan deras dua hari, banyak jalan di Jakarta kebanjiran.

rows.en: There was a strong earthquake in Lombok last night.
rows.id: Ada gempa bumi kuat di Lombok tadi malam.

rows.en: The storm closed the harbour, so the ferries didn't leave.
rows.id: Badai membuat pelabuhan ditutup, jadi kapal feri tidak berangkat.

rows.en: During the heatwave in Europe, it was over 40 degrees.
rows.id: Saat gelombang panas di Eropa, suhunya lebih dari 40 derajat.

rows.en: The haze from the forest fires is very bad today.
rows.id: Kabut asap dari kebakaran hutan sangat parah hari ini.

blocks.text:
**'Jakarta banjir' is not 'Jakarta is flood'.** In Indonesian *banjir* works like a verb or adjective, but in English **flood** is a noun (*a flood*) or a verb (*it floods*). Say:
- **There's a flood in Jakarta.** / **There was a flood in Jakarta.**
- **Jakarta floods every year.** / **The streets flooded.**

The same with *gempa*: **There was an earthquake**, never *'it earthquaked'*.

id.text:
**'Jakarta banjir' bukan 'Jakarta is flood'.** Dalam bahasa Indonesia *banjir* bisa jadi kata kerja atau kata sifat, tapi dalam bahasa Inggris **flood** adalah kata benda (*a flood*) atau kata kerja (*it floods*). Katakan:
- **There's a flood in Jakarta.** / **There was a flood in Jakarta.**
- **Jakarta floods every year.** / **The streets flooded.**

Sama dengan *gempa*: **There was an earthquake**, jangan pernah *'it earthquaked'*.

blocks.prompt: It rained very hard all afternoon in Bandung. Choose the natural phrase: There was ___ in Bandung this afternoon.
blocks.explain: Hujan deras = heavy rain. 'Big rain' is a word-by-word translation of hujan besar, and 'strong water' isn't English.

id.prompt: Hujan sangat deras sepanjang sore di Bandung. Pilih frasa yang alami: There was ___ in Bandung this afternoon.
id.explain: Hujan deras = heavy rain. 'Big rain' adalah terjemahan kata per kata dari hujan besar, dan 'strong water' bukan bahasa Inggris.

resources.title: Learn English Words With Pictures: Natural Disasters
resources.note: Twelve disaster words with pictures, short definitions and audio, including flood, drought, earthquake, landslide and forest fire. It also has words this lesson doesn't teach, like hurricane, blizzard and avalanche.

id.note: Dua belas kata bencana dengan gambar, definisi singkat dan audio, termasuk flood, drought, earthquake, landslide dan forest fire. Ada juga kata yang tidak diajarkan di pelajaran ini, seperti hurricane, blizzard dan avalanche.

resources.title: Tackling overtourism
resources.note: A LearnEnglish Teens page with a short video report on overtourism (Bali is one of the places mentioned), its transcript and exercises. It's for teenagers at B2–C1, so it's above this lesson's level: read the transcript if the video is fast.

id.intro: Hai! Hari ini kamu akan belajar kata-kata untuk membicarakan berita: polusi udara dan sampah plastik, wisatawan dan budaya setempat, banjir, kekeringan dan gunung berapi. Kita latih dalam situasi nyata di Indonesia, dari kabut asap di Kalimantan sampai wisatawan di Borobudur. Pemanasan: apa masalah lingkungan terbesar di kotamu?

assessment.env-1: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Everyone should saving energy at home.
assessment.env-2: Lengkapi dengan satu kata: Jakarta has a lot of air ___ because of the traffic and the factories. On bad days the sky is grey and people wear masks.
assessment.env-3: Lengkapi dengan reduce, reuse atau recycle: Rina always takes her own bag to the supermarket because she wants to ___ the amount of plastic she uses.
assessment.env-4: Perbaiki kesalahannya: In August, Labuan Bajo is full of foreign tourist.
assessment.env-5: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Monas is a famous tourism object in Jakarta.
assessment.env-6: Lengkapi dengan satu kata bahasa Inggris: Too much water is a flood. Too little water for a long time, when there is no rain for months and the rice fields become dry, is a ___.
assessment.env-7: Lengkapi dengan satu kata: Mount Merapi ___ again last night. Hot ash and smoke went high into the sky, and people in nearby villages left their homes.
